description: Labeled cases for figure_check.py — figure/table existence, numbering and caption lint. Four defects per kind: a figure the prose mentions but never embeds, an embedded figure nothing refers to, a number used twice, and a gap in the sequence; plus a figure embedded without a caption in analysis/captions.md. The negatives are the shapes that look broken and are not: a range mention (Figures 1-3), the same figure referred to several times, and a fenced code block that happens to contain image syntax.

cases.comment: The defect that survives to print most often: a figure is promised in the prose and the image was never added.

mutations.breaks: A figure the prose promises but never embeds stops being reported — the defect most likely to reach a reviewer.
An embedded figure nothing refers to stops being reported.
Two figures sharing a number stop being reported, so the build silently renders one caption twice.
replace: duplicates = [{"num": n, "locations": v} for n, v in embedded.items() if len(v) > 1]

mutations.breaks: A cut figure that left a hole in the numbering stops being reported.
replace: gaps = [n for n in range(base_ints[0], base_ints[-1] + 1) if n not in base_ints]

mutations.breaks: A figure absent from analysis/captions.md stops being reported, so it ships without a caption.
replace: if cap_names["Figure"] and stem not in cap_names["Figure"]

mutations.breaks: Embed syntax shown inside a fenced example counts as a real figure, so a Methods section documenting the convention reports orphans.
A caption printed before a lower-numbered one stops being reported. Gap, duplicate and mention checks are all order-blind, so nothing else covers it.
replace: if peak is not None and n < peak:

mutations.breaks: A range whose ends are equal or inverted goes back to contributing nothing and reporting nothing — a broken cross-reference becomes invisible rather than wrong.
